headline: Northrop Grumman scores big. SpaceX delivers again. True Anomaly raises cash.
deck: This week, major contracts and funding rounds highlight the shifting dynamics in space procurement and investment.

stories.head: Northrop Grumman grabs $398 million from Space Force
stories.body: The Space Force has awarded Northrop Grumman a $398 million contract for a satellite aimed at testing protected communications. This move underscores the military's ongoing need for reliable communication channels in space—because even the cosmos can’t survive on spotty Wi-Fi. With this contract, Northrop is solidifying its role as a key player in defense-related space operations.
stories.soWhat: It’s a reminder that in the space game, reliable communications are as vital as rocket launches.

stories.head: SpaceX completes another successful cargo mission
stories.body: SpaceX successfully launched the CRS-34 cargo mission to the ISS, delivering nearly 3,000 kilograms of supplies. This mission continues to demonstrate SpaceX's operational reliability, as astronauts can't live on freeze-dried food alone. With each successful launch, SpaceX inches closer to normalizing its role as the go-to logistics provider for low Earth orbit.
stories.soWhat: SpaceX's consistent performance is making it harder for competitors to justify their own launch delays.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190 million for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, pushing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This funding will bolster its capabilities in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, reflecting a growing interest in safeguarding assets in orbit. The infusion of capital comes at a time when the DoD is increasingly focused on ensuring the security of its space assets.
stories.soWhat: In a sector where cash flow often trumps innovation, True Anomaly's funding is a clear signal that investors are betting on security over shiny tech.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on the ESA-China SMILE mission
watchlist.body: Launching on May 19, this mission could provide valuable data on Earth's magnetic shield, which might influence future space missions.

watchlist.title: Virgin Galactic's commercial service launch
watchlist.body: With claims to begin commercial service this year, it will be interesting to see if they can finally deliver on the promise of suborbital tourism.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris constellation bid progress
watchlist.body: The collaboration on a tactical SDA constellation could reshape defense capabilities, so expect updates as the bid develops.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension impact
watchlist.body: With a $480 million extension, Palantir's software prowess in defense will be under scrutiny as they continue to secure government contracts.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.

tickers.note: Northrop Grumman's contract win underscores its strong position in defense procurement.
Virgin Galactic's insistence on starting commercial flights this year raises questions about their operational readiness.
True Anomaly's funding round reflects a growing focus on co-orbital security solutions.
Palantir's TITAN extension shows that software contracts are becoming as critical as hardware in defense.
